title: OAuth sign-in with PKCE
objective: Learners follow a mobile app sign-in message by message and see why the access token never passes through the browser, and why PKCE makes a stolen authorization code useless.
assumptions: The app is a public client: a mobile app with no client secret
The attacker is a malicious app that registered the same myapp:// redirect scheme (the threat PKCE was designed for, RFC 7636 section 1)
Simplified: state, nonce, scopes and token expiry are left out
Endpoint paths and the myapp:// scheme are illustrative
Timings are playback seconds, not real durations

learnerPrompts.predict: Turn on the malicious app and turn PKCE off. Who ends up holding your access token, and at which step could the auth server have stopped it?
learnerPrompts.explain: The browser carries the authorization code but never the token or the verifier. Why does that make a stolen code worthless when PKCE is on?
